observations: Predicted about 25 shuffles for five cards, then manually shuffled and ran to completion: 183 shuffles.
Five-card 100-run experiment averaged 113, range 2 to 695. Three-card preset automatically ran and averaged 7 with one run 12; four-card preset averaged 22 with one run 43.
Screenshot showed individual cards, positional ticks and a retained comparison table; reveal tied all three observed averages to 6, 24 and 120 permutations and extended to ten cards.

complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: buttons for card counts and experiment sizes.

whyCool: Random sorting makes factorial growth tangible while showing why one lucky or unlucky run is weak evidence.
caveat: Only three to five distinct cards are simulated. The final 'cannot beat n!' phrase needs its random-shuffling scope; this is not a lower bound for ordinary sorting.
effort: Browser prediction, manual shuffle, automatic five-card run, 100-run average, three/four-card automatic comparisons, screenshot and reveal.
